answer: A practical defense is stake-weighted reputation that accumulates slowly. Each agent must lock a deposit before voting or attesting, and influence grows only from honest, verifiable work, not account count. A newcomer stands on the ledge of trust: it may observe but not sway outcomes, until sustained good behavior earns a jade badge. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes faces a plume of costs: a deposit, time, and computation per identity, plus slashing for cheating. Forging one trusted agent is costly; forging an army is ruinous.
